title: Kula Disaster Recovery Update Meeting: December 12, 2023

recap.headline: Kula fire recovery update: debris removal, rebuild permits, lead and air testing
recap.in_60_seconds: County, state and federal agencies held their weekly Upcountry meeting on Kula wildfire recovery. The Army Corps of Engineers reported debris fully removed from 18 of 24 enrolled properties. Public Works said rebuild permits can be submitted now but cannot be issued until debris removal is verified, with no fee waivers and an emergency permit office targeted for March or early April. Health officials reported no asbestos in air samples and no elevated blood lead among 25 Kula adults tested. Eight people asked questions, mostly about neighbors' damaged but unburned properties, permit delays, temporary housing and insurance living expenses. A visit by the state insurance commissioner and soil testing for neighboring properties remain unresolved.

parts.title: Opening and MEMA update
presented: Q&A limited to one question per person
Door hangers went out to notify neighbors of debris work
Team Rubicon returns in the new year to clear wind-downed logs
MEMA seeking funding for water tanks and fire planning; no timelines yet

next.what: Team Rubicon returns for larger debris cuts
Timeline for water tank and fire planning projects

parts.title: Army Corps of Engineers debris removal update
parts.presenter: Commander, Army Corps Recovery Field Office
presented: 24 properties enrolled, up from 21
Debris fully removed from 18; soil sampling done at 17
2 properties needed more debris removed
3 completed packets sent to the County and FEMA, done right after each property to speed rebuilding

parts.title: Rights of entry and debris mission scope
parts.presenter: FEMA debris mission task force leader
presented: 24 of 24 Upcountry rights of entry received
Some rights of entry came from homes with no damage; the program is for destroyed homes
FEMA funding expanded to foundations, vehicles, demolition, commercial sites and soil sampling
Rights of entry are not the way to request general assistance

parts.title: Rebuild permitting
presented: Permits can be submitted now but cannot be issued until debris removal is verified under Ordinance 5562
Average permit takes about 300 days; fire parcels will be flagged for priority
No fee waivers, to keep eligibility for federal reimbursement
Permits issued since August 8, 2018 can be reissued; rebuilds must meet current codes; temporary structure process being adjusted

next.what: Emergency permitting office run by a contracted firm opens

parts.title: Department of Health air and lead update
presented: Second week of air samples (Nov 16-22) showed no asbestos and metals below action levels
65 sensors and monitors on Maui and Lānaʻi, including 25 in Kula and Makawao
Of 272 Maui adults tested for blood lead, 25 from Kula had no elevated levels; 4 elevated elsewhere
Children and pregnant women exposed to ash urged to get lead screening; flu shots encouraged

next.what: Air sample results posted weekly online instead of press releases
Some Kula air monitors move to Lahaina

parts.title: FEMA deadlines and wildfire contamination expert
parts.presenter: FEMA official and FEMA subject matter expert
presented: FEMA application deadline passed yesterday; 60-day period allowed with justification
SBA offers a 45-day grace period
Expert reviewed Kula and Lahaina sites and sampling protocols and called the data encouraging and beyond standard practice

parts.title: U.S. Health and Human Services services
parts.presenter: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services staff
presented: Human services such as child care and TANF
Support for hospitals, teachers and schools
CDC environmental health expert arriving this week
Confidential behavioral health support available

raised.concern: Whether rebuilds will require arsenic-treated wood
Whether the code's approval-by-default rule for emergency rebuilds will apply, since people cannot wait 300 days
A neighbor near burned homes tested close to the lead threshold; neighbors should be notified and tested
Damaged but unburned neighboring homes with blown-in ash and debris are denied rights of entry and soil testing
Whether container homes can be placed as temporary housing without permits, and the size limit
What MEMA is changing to prepare for future disasters, including fire maps for the public
When the insurance commissioner will come, as insurance living expenses may run out before rebuilds
Whether backflow preventers will be required and Water Supply permit reviews sped up

answered.said: The department does not regulate building materials; arsenic-based treatment is no longer used in wood.
The code requires no particular material, only one that meets code.
A seven-day turnaround provision exists in the code, but its age and use are unclear.
MEMA will take the lead notification concern.
Temporary structures need a permit involving about a dozen agencies; his deputy is vetting temporary housing products.

answered.who: FEMA debris mission task force leader
answered.said: FEMA does not sample or remove ash blown onto neighbors' yards; the cleanup list follows EPA Phase 1, but significant damage may warrant a look.
MEMA is condensing its playbook, planning community education and evacuation routes, building an incident management team, listing water tank projects and adding GIS mapping staff.
The insurance commissioner's visit kept getting pushed back; he will come but no date is set.
He is unsure about backflow preventers; Water Supply is pressed daily to prepare for rebuild permits.

next.what: Insurance commissioner attends a Kula meeting

answered.said: FEMA does not cover neighbors, so the State may need to step in; she will follow up on an insurance extension request made to the Governor in August.

next.what: Follow-up with FEMA and the Governor on neighbors and insurance

parts.title: Closing
presented: Residents referred to the MauiRecovers.org site and its Crisis Cleanup hotline
No meeting the week of December 26

bills.name: Ordinance 5562
bills.what: Bars building permit issuance on fire-affected parcels until debris removal is verified.

open_questions.question: Will damaged but unburned neighboring properties get soil testing or debris removal, and from which agency?
Will the code's quick approval-by-default provision apply to emergency rebuild permits?
When will the state insurance commissioner meet Kula residents about living expense coverage?
Will rebuilt lots need backflow preventers?
What size limit applies to temporary structures without a permit, 200 or 400 square feet?
